requirement:
The book's coverage overview lists current source files carrying
`habeas:coverage` annotations on their file roots or explicitly declared
functions and methods. Every such annotation is browsable, including
annotations with missing or rejected reviews and annotations whose measured
coverage already meets its obligations. Listing an annotation does not
establish whether it is a currently needed or accepted exception.
rationale:
The three marked tests cover every obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.combined`.

**Annotations on file roots and on explicitly declared functions and methods are listed.**
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[documented_items_are_counted_once_with_browsable_directory_and_file_groups]` uses file-root annotations (`code.rs` shows "File root") and function annotations (`fn[one]`, `fn[direct]`, `fn[second]`, `fn[unexplained]`). It asserts each item's file, line and selector, the "7 documented source items" count, the per-directory groups and the per-file cards.
- It also checks that `src/pass.rs`, which has no annotation, is absent.
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[documentation_includes_non_rust_functions_methods_and_plain_file_roots]` covers Python (`def[work]`), TypeScript (`function[work]`, class `method[work]`) and a plain-text file root (`notes.txt`). It asserts all of them are listed, with "4 documented source items".

**Every annotation is browsable, whatever its review or measurement state.**
- `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[book_browses_all_proposals_while_cli_checks_reviews_and_measurements]` renders the book with a missing review. It asserts `fn[b]` is listed with "Recorded review: Missing".
- It then re-renders with each recorded determination: true ("Recorded true"), false ("Recorded false", the rejected case) and FIXME ("Recorded FIXME"). Each time it asserts the file card and `fn[b]` are still listed.
- It raises the measured counts so the CLI report passes and asserts `fn[b]` is still listed. This is the case where measured coverage already meets its obligations.
- It deletes the profile so the CLI check fails and asserts the render is identical to the covered render.
- It asserts that unannotated `fn[a]` is not listed.

**The overview reflects the current source.** The last step of that test rewrites `code.rs`. The render then shows "No tracked justification is present." and no longer shows the old justification, so the list follows the source as it is now.

**Listing does not establish that an annotation is needed or accepted.**
- The tests assert that verdict-like content is absent: "CI would", "instrumented lines covered", `gap-percentage`, `gap-verdict` and `data-status=`.
- The directories `vendor` and `docs_only` appear regardless of any acceptance status.

Handling of removed or unreadable files falls under other requirements. `fn[missing_and_unreadable_sources_produce_overview_diagnostics]` covers it, so it is not needed here.

I found no obligation without a test and no assertion that contradicts the text.
